Latest release · Lotus Root 12.5.6 · 22 Nov 2026

Encrypted links between nodes, a node in the browser, Lotus Desktop

Nodes now encrypt the links between them, the node's pages carry a small Lotus node that runs in the visitor's browser, and Lotus Desktop arrives: one app to mine, hold a wallet and vote with RANK.

⬇ Download 12.5.6What is newQuick start

until Napoleon (about: it activates on the median time of the blocks)

Napoleon, 2026-12-21 20:50 UTCEvery node must run 12.5.1 or later before then. Earlier versions, 12.4.x included, do not follow the chain after the fork. Upgrade guide

What is new in 12.5.6

  • Indexer: a failed rollback could stop block processing; upgrade recommended.
  • Pools: a node whose ledger fell out of line repairs itself, and the ASIC proxy pools are the ones the operator lists.

Encrypted connections between nodes

Two 12.5.6 nodes encrypt the link between them; with an older node the link stays as it was.
Nothing to set up. The peer list shows which links are encrypted.

A Lotus node in the browser

The node's pages turn the visitor's browser into a small Lotus node that checks block headers itself. The web wallet uses it, and opens Lotus Qt and lotusd wallet files too. One setting lets an operator turn it off for every visitor.
Your browser checks the chain itself instead of trusting one server.

Lotus Desktop, first release

One app to mine with your GPU, hold a wallet and vote with RANK on X (Linux for now). It is also a small peer of the network that checks block headers itself. Your keys stay on your computer: write down the recovery words or save a backup file before you put coins in.
Mine and keep what you earn in one app, with keys on your own computer.

Secure WebSocket with automatic certificates

for operators who turn them on.
Pages served over HTTPS can reach your node, with a free certificate it renews itself.

Checksums: SHA256SUMS · every file and the Docker images: release page

Quick start

Docker 
docker pull ghcr.io/lotusdevorg/lotusd:12.5.6
docker run -d --name lotusd -v lotus-data:/data ghcr.io/lotusdevorg/lotusd:12.5.6
Linux 
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/LotusDevOrg/lotusd-releases/releases/download/v12.5.6/SHA256SUMS
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/LotusDevOrg/lotusd-releases/releases/download/v12.5.6/lotus-binaries-12.5.6-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS     # must print: OK
tar -xzf lotus-binaries-12.5.6-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
./lotus-binaries-12.5.6-linux-x86_64/lotusd -version
macOS

The same steps with lotus-binaries-12.5.6-macos-x86_64.tar.gz; check with shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS. macOS asks for confirmation before the first launch (the binaries are not notarised).

Windows

Download lotus-binaries-12.5.6-windows-x86_64.zip and SHA256SUMS. In PowerShell, Get-FileHash .\lotus-binaries-12.5.6-windows-x86_64.zip -Algorithm SHA256 must give the value on that file's line. Then unzip.
